To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

crop models need to incorporate the following: (i) a better description of how plants respond to extreme events such as drought and heat stress; (ii) a more complete understanding of the interactions between the different components of the Kaya identity, including their responses to climate change; (iii) a better understanding of the interactions and responses of the different components of plant growth to the environment, including the effects of climate change.

1) crop models are not yet able to simulate crop responses to extreme events, 2) crop models are able to simulate crop response to atmospheric CO2 concentration changes, but not the effects of rising temperatures, 3) the Kaya- Porter identity is a useful tool for deconstruction of crop resource use efficiency into component identities and 4) deconstruction can be used to identify the effects of changing climatic variables on the component identities.

crop simulation models are currently inadequate for the future, that there is a need to develop a more holistic approach to modelling crop processes and that the Kaya-Identity approach to deconstructing crop processes may be a way forward.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how plants and ecosystems function, and how they respond to changes in the environment.
the development and use of crop models for understanding and predicting the responses of crops and crop systems to climate variability and change.
the responses of plants to the environment and how these responses can be simulated by mathematical models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we do not know how to model the effects of changing climate and climate variability on crops and crop yields, but we do have a few ideas.

we need to deconstruct crop simulation models and crop processes into their constituent identities and then reassemble the models and processes, with a view to understanding the effects of climate change and the effects of crops on climate change, and the feedbacks between the two.
we need to understand the effects of changing climatic variables on the processes that determine the growth and yield of crops.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
crop models are not yet good enough to be used for the purposes of predicting the effects of climatic changes on crops, but that there is no reason why we cannot make them better.
the future of crop simulation modelling is in the future.

crop simulation models are a very powerful way to explore the effects of climate and climate change on crop production, and that they can do this in a way that is more realistic, and hence more credible to the wider community, than simple empirical models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Kaya-Identity approach is useful for deconstructing crop processes, and it may be a useful approach for deconstructing other complex processes.
the current crop modelling approaches are not adequate for the future.
the Kaya- Porter identity can be used to deconstruct the resource use efficiencies of a crop, which can be examined in terms of their response to climate and climatically changing variables.
